hints: Use Pythagoras for its modulus and identify its exact angle from the fourth-quadrant reference triangle, stating an acceptable argument convention.
walkthrough:
Determine the argument $\arg u$:
Since the real part is $1 > 0$ and the imaginary part is $-\sqrt{3} < 0$, $u$ lies in the fourth quadrant of the Argand diagram:
$$\arg u = -\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{1}\right) = -\dfrac{1}{3}\pi \quad \left(\text{or } -60^\circ\right)$$

hints: Use the polar form from part (i) and De Moivre's theorem to cube both the modulus and argument.
Evaluate the exact sine and cosine at the tripled argument, then substitute the resulting real value into $u^3+8$.
walkthrough:
Express $u$ in polar form using the modulus and argument from part (i):
$$u = 2\left[\cos\left(-\dfrac{1}{3}\pi\right) + \mathrm{i}\sin\left(-\dfrac{1}{3}\pi\right)\right]$$

Apply De Moivre's theorem to compute $u^3$:
$$u^3 = 2^3 \left[\cos\left(3 \times \left(-\dfrac{1}{3}\pi\right)\right) + \mathrm{i}\sin\left(3 \times \left(-\dfrac{1}{3}\pi\right)\right)\right] = 8\left[\cos(-\pi) + \mathrm{i}\sin(-\pi)\right]$$

hints: Draw the closed disc with centre $u=(1,-\sqrt3)$ and radius $2$; it passes through the origin.
Shade only the part of the disc on or to the right of this line, keeping both boundaries solid.
walkthrough:
Identify the boundary and region for the first inequality $|z - u| \le 2$:
- The locus $|z - u| = 2$ represents a circle with centre $(1, -\sqrt{3})$ in the fourth quadrant and radius $2$.
- The distance from the centre $(1, -\sqrt{3})$ to the origin is $\sqrt{1^2 + (-\sqrt{3})^2} = 2$, so this circle passes precisely through the origin $(0, 0)$.
- The inequality $|z - u| \le 2$ defines the closed disc consisting of the circle and its interior.

Identify the boundary and region for the second inequality $\operatorname{Re}z \ge 2$:
- $\operatorname{Re}z = 2$ is the vertical line passing through $x = 2$.
- The inequality $\operatorname{Re}z \ge 2$ defines the half-plane lying on and to the right of this vertical line.

Determine the intersection of the two regions:
- The rightmost point of the circle is at $x = 1 + 2 = 3$, so the vertical line $x = 2$ intersects the circular boundary.
- The required region is the circular segment inside or on the circle of centre $(1, -\sqrt{3})$ and radius $2$ that lies to the right of or on the vertical line $\operatorname{Re}z = 2$.
Shade this intersecting circular segment, drawing both the circular arc boundary and the vertical line boundary $x = 2$ as solid lines to reflect non-strict inequalities.
